texto_para_tela: 15.5 MILLION ACRE-FEET / ≈ 6 WEEKS OF AVERAGE FLOW AT THE DALLES / ≈ 3.5 MONTHS AT BIRCHBANK
credito_sugerido: Source: Columbia River Treaty, Art. II · Alpha Point calculation: Water Survey of Canada (station 08NE049), USGS (14105700). Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence – Canada.
nota: Refeito (F102, F105). As duas médias de The Dalles dão ≈ 6 semanas. Em Birchbank dá 3.61 meses: 'closer to three and a half months' (a voz) está certo; na tela, '≈ 3.5 MONTHS' arredonda para baixo — '≈ 3.6 MONTHS' ou 'ABOUT 3½ MONTHS' é a forma do redator. F107: BC Hydro 2026, p. 7.
conversoes: com a média de 1974–2024 (176,486 cfs): 44.3 dias = 6.33 semanas

Alpha Point calculation: Water Survey of Canada (station 08NE049), USGS (14105700)
texto_aprovado: For another, look at what the dams can hold. Together, the three treaty lakes in Canada can store as much water as the whole river carries past The Dalles in about six weeks. Measured against the river as it runs through British Columbia, near the border, that's closer to three and a half months. Then the lakes are full, and the rest of the river keeps coming. So Canada can't turn the Columbia off. What it can do, under plans agreed with the United States, is decide when a big share of that water comes down. Remember that Canadian gauge?
